text: Storyteller is the fifth studio album by American singer and songwriter Carrie Underwood, released on October 23, 2015, through Sony Music Nashville. Following the success of her fourth studio album, Blown Away (2012), Underwood began working on Storyteller in early 2014 but suspended most of the work due to her pregnancy with her first child. She released her first greatest hits album, Greatest Hits: Decade #1, on December 9, 2014, to great success. After giving birth in February 2015, she returned to the studio in early 2015 to complete the album. Met with mostly positive reviews from critics, Storyteller became a commercial success and set multiple records, debuting at number two on the Billboard 200, making Underwood the only country artist in history to have all of her first five studio albums debut at number one or two, and achieving a number one debut on the Top Country Albums chart, making her the only artist to have six consecutive number one albums on that chart. The album also performed well internationally, debuting at number four in Australia, number three in Canada, and number thirteen in the United Kingdom. As of October 2016, it was certified Platinum by the RIAA, marking Underwood's sixth consecutive album to reach Platinum or multi-Platinum status. The album produced five singles: "Smoke Break," "Heartbeat," "Chaser," "Church Bells," and "Dirty Laundry." "Heartbeat" and "Church Bells" reached number one consecutively on the Billboard Country Airplay chart, while "Smoke Break" peaked at number two. "Smoke Break," "Heartbeat," and "Dirty Laundry" topped the Billboard Canada Country chart, and all four of these songs received Platinum or multi-Platinum certifications. Underwood described Storyteller as more laid-back and more twangy than Blown Away, working with frequent collaborators including Hillary Lindsey, Ashley Gorley, Chris DeStefano, David Hodges, Brett James, and Mark Bright, as well as new collaborators Liz Rose, Zach Crowell, and Jay Joyce. This album marks Underwood's last release under Arista Nashville and Sony Music Group, following her new deal with Universal Music Group's Capitol Nashville. The cover artwork shows Underwood in a "dreamy" setting, seated on a pale floor with a soft "haze," wearing red, bejeweled cowboy boots and a flowing ivory shirt with red embroidery, her hair styled "slightly messy" and makeup "simple." Underwood emphasized that the album introduced "some new ideas" without a dramatic stylistic break, maintaining continuity while showing growth, describing it as a "little bit of a shift" rather than a radical change. She noted that each song has its own space, sound, and feel, with a "rock twang" tone, and that many songs are more traditional and "twangy" than her earlier work, reflecting her attachment to the storytelling aspect of country music. Personal experience, particularly motherhood, influenced the album's themes, though she stressed that it was not forced and that the inspiration "just kind of happened," adding that her son brought a sense of "life magic" into the creative process. On August 20, 2015, Underwood announced the album's title and release date via a live Facebook stream, revealed the track listing on September 9 through Instagram, and performed "Smoke Break" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on September 10. She performed "Church Bells" at the Apple Music Festival in London on September 21 and returned to headline the C2C: Country to Country festival for the first time since 2013, performing in London, Dublin, Glasgow, Oslo, and Stockholm. On October 22, she announced a performance at the 2015 American Music Awards on November 22. On January 27, 2016, it was revealed that Underwood and Sam Hunt were nominated for Best Country Solo Performance and Best Country Album, respectively, and would perform together at the 2016 Grammy Awards, performing Hunt's "Take Your Time" before transitioning into Underwood's "Heartbeat" and returning to the chorus of "Take Your Time." She performed "Church Bells" at the 2016 Academy of Country Music Awards on April 3 and at the CMT Awards on June 8. On May 19, Sunday Night Football announced that Underwood would perform "Waiting All Day for Sunday Night" at the fourth season of the show. In October 2017, Underwood released a live concert film titled Carrie Underwood: The Storyteller Tour — Stories in the Round, Live from Madison Square Garden, recorded during her October 2016 stop at Madison Square Garden, featuring 22 songs from her catalog, including 17 chart-topping singles, and highlighting the tour's 360-degree stage design and large-scale production. "Smoke Break," the lead single, was first teased on August 20, 2015, and released the next day, produced by Jay Joyce and written by Underwood, DeStefano, and Lindsey. It set a record for the largest first-week radio adds in Country Aircheck history with 145 Mediabase adds, 159 total Billboard and Country Aircheck stations, debuted at number 36 on the Hot Country Songs chart, and peaked at number 4, reaching number 2 on the Country Airplay chart and number one on the Country Digital Songs chart. The music video was teased on August 23 and released shortly after. "Heartbeat," released as a promotional single on October 9, made its official radio debut on November 30, co-written and produced by Zach Crowell, featured background vocals by Sam Hunt, and had its music video released on December 1. It sold 23,000 copies, debuted at number 26 on Hot Country Songs, and reached number two on the chart, peaking at number one on Country Airplay by October 26. "Chaser" was released exclusively to UK radio on April 1, 2016, as the third single; "Church Bells," released to country radio on April 11, reached number two on Hot Country Songs and number one on Country Airplay and was nominated for Best Country Solo Performance at the 59th Grammy Awards. "Dirty Laundry," confirmed for release on August 11, was first released as a promotional single on August 12 and sent to country radio on September 6, produced by Jay Joyce and written by Crowell, Ashley Gorley, and Lindsey; its music video, directed by Shane C. Drake, premiered on October 12 at Entertainment Tonight, presented in stark black-and-white to symbolize themes of infidelity and instinctual behavior. Underwood performed "Dirty Laundry" at the 50th CMA Awards on November 2. Commercially, it peaked at number two on Country Airplay and number three on Hot Country Songs. "Renegade Runaway," released as a promotional single on October 16, peaked at number 34 on Hot Country Songs, co-written by Underwood, DeStefano, and Lindsey. "What I Never Knew I Always Wanted," released on October 19, peaked at number 32 on Hot Country Songs. Underwood began the Storyteller Tour: Stories in the Round on January 30, 2016, in Jacksonville, Florida, first teasing the tour on October 27, 2015. The first leg concluded in London, Ontario by May 31, 2016, with the tour scheduled during her husband Mike Fisher's NHL season. In April 2016, additional fall dates were announced, resuming on September 4 in Spokane, Washington, with Easton Corbin, the Swon Brothers, and Keith Urban as opening acts. The fall leg included major arena stops in Los Angeles, Nashville, and New York City. The tour concluded on November 28 in Salt Lake City, Utah, with a total of 92 shows and approximately one million attendees, including sold-out dates at Madison Square Garden, Staples Center, Bridgestone Arena, and Air Canada Centre. The tour grossed $54.6 million and had overall attendance exceeding 800,000, as reported in a Billboard Hot Tours recap. According to Metacritic, Storyteller received "generally favorable reviews" with a weighted average score of 74 out of 100 from 9 critics. Stephen Thomas Erlewine of AllMusic noted the album "demands attention and it deserves it, too," while Sarah Rodman of The Boston Globe called it Underwood's best album yet. Billboard's Jewly Hight highlighted Underwood's authority and the album's reconciliation of her "Midwestern girl-next-door" and "imperious diva" images within a "freshened-up aesthetic frames." Robert Christgau of Vice praised the songwriting, noting more "good tales" than her greatest hits album and that she allows songs to "narrate for themselves," though he noted she "still oversings sometimes." Critics like Jon Caramanica of the New York Times questioned the album's expressive sharpness, finding it lacking "bite or pulp" and primarily serving as launch pads for Underwood's "ballistic-missile voice," while Stuart Henderson of Exclaim! described it as "more than halfway boring" and argued that its heavy use of "booming bass," "pounding drums," "huge vocals," and "wailing guitars" dulled its emotional impact. Storyteller received a nomination for Album of the Year at both the 2016 American Country Countdown Awards and the 50th annual CMA Awards. At the 2016 American Music Awards, the album and Underwood were nominated for Favorite Album – Country and Artist of the Year, with the album winning, marking Underwood's fifth win in that category. In the United States, Storyteller debuted at number two on the Billboard 200, selling 177,000 album-equivalent units, including 164,000 pure sales, and made Underwood the only country artist with all first five studio albums debuting at number one or two. It also debuted at number one on the Top Country Albums chart, securing her record as the only artist with six consecutive number one albums on that chart. It held number two on the Billboard 200 in its second week, moving 81,000 units, including over 73,000 album copies, and returned to number one on the Top Country Albums chart on December 19. It was certified Gold by the RIAA on December 4, 2015, for over 500,000 shipments, and was certified Platinum in October 2016, becoming her sixth Platinum album. As of April 2017, it had sold 752,100 copies in the U.S. Outside the U.S., it debuted at number three in Canada, number four in Australia, number six in Scotland, and number thirteen in the UK, marking her second top twenty album in the country. Four of the album's songs, excluding the five singles, also charted on Hot Country Songs: "The Girl You Think I Am" at number 38 and "Like I'll Never Love You Again" at number 39; "Relapse" peaked at number 48 with 4,000 copies and "Choctaw County Affair" at number 68 with 3,000 copies.
